value.body: A fitness trainer plans exercise programmes and supervises clients at gyms, sports clubs, residential societies, corporate wellness centres or online. Some work as strength and conditioning staff for teams. Work is often in early-morning and evening shifts, with most time spent training clients.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.P.E.S. / B.P.Ed, or a fitness certification

items.label: Students in B.P.Ed. programmes
items.note: Plus ~23,000 in B.P.E.; many fitness trainers enter through certifications instead

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start as floor trainers at gyms and build a client base, or join fitness chains with their own training programmes. A physical education or sport-science degree helps for strength and conditioning roles with teams.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is private and pay often depends on client numbers.
Certifications are common but not standardised.
Next roles: senior trainer, strength and conditioning coach, own studio.

competition.note: B.P.Ed graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
